title: Homepage leadline + hero slate: velocity, trust, and inference economics
body:
Purpose
- Create a compact leadline + hero bundle that speaks to engineering buyers (builds trust) while still landing the product-level value props (latency, cost, predictability).
- Ship 3 distinct voice directions for rapid A/B through next week.
- Provide rationale, evidence hooks, and primary CTA per variant so engineers can self-serve.

Context and constraints
- Audience: engineers/ML engineers evaluating inference platforms; PMs who own product cost; infra/platform teams.
- Primary landing goal: sign-up for self-serve API + gating for enterprise interest (dedicated/private).
- Secondary goal: get teams to run our cost/latency calculator or request a Dedicated capacity demo.
- Need to show credible operational proof without heavy marketing-speak. Use concrete signals (SLA, percent improvements, latency numbers, case study blurbs).
- Avoid generic "AI platform" jargon; emphasize inference as a production problem (SLOs, cost per token, predictable rollout).

Three voice directions (short descriptions + why)
1) Engineering Assurance (technical first)
  - Leadline idea: "Inference that behaves — predictable latency, sane unit cost."
  - Tone: concise, confident, technical.
  - Why: resonates with infra teams worried about tail latency and cost variance.
  - Proof hooks to include: per-route latency SLO, canary rollouts, KV cache and batching savings (example: "up to 4x lower per-token cost with caching + batching on typical chat workloads").
  - CTA: "Try the latency demo" (links to interactive playground with tokens and latency breakdown).

2) Cost-first pragmatist (econ/ops)
  - Leadline idea: "Pay for inference, not for surprise bills."
  - Tone: practical, ROI-focused.
  - Why: procurement and product leads care about predictable spend; startups care about controlling burn.
  - Proof hooks: unit economics calculator, dedicated capacity pricing snapshot, testimonial snippet: "Reduced inference spend by 37% in month 1".
  - CTA: "Calculate your inference run-rate" (leads to quick input form).

3) Resilience & Compliance (enterprise-friendly)
  - Leadline idea: "Keep LLM features online — even when models or regions fail."
  - Tone: reassured, authoritative, enterprise.
  - Why: enterprise buyers need fallbacks, private deployment, and auditability.
  - Proof hooks: private VPC option, KMS/HSM mention, audit logs, 99.95% uptime SLA.
  - CTA: "Request dedicated deployment" (leads to sales contact + checklist).

Hero copy variants (concise snippets)
- Eng Assurance Variant A: "Predictable LLM inference — low tail latency, deterministic cost."
- Eng Assurance Variant B: "Same API for hosted, dedicated, and private inference — ship once, run anywhere."
- Cost Pragmatist Variant A: "Control token spend with smart batching and caching — measurable savings on day one."
- Cost Pragmatist Variant B: "Unit costs you can forecast. Controls you can enforce."
- Resilience Variant A: "Model fallbacks, region failover, and audit trails — keep product features online."
- Resilience Variant B: "Private deployments with platform-grade SLAs and key management."

Subhead + supporting blurbs (mix-and-match)
- "One API. Three deployment modes. Zero surprises."
- "Optimize latency, cost, and reliability with per-route controls and transparent metrics."
- "Build features that rely on inference without building inference ops."

Microcopy and badges to test in hero area
- Short badges under hero (3): "<latency> 99th-p90 to p99 SLOs", "<savings> Typical 2–4x effective cost drop with caching", "<deployment> Hosted · Dedicated · Private"
- Include a tiny trust line: "Used in production by startups and regulated enterprises."

CTA matrix (primary and secondary per variant)
- Eng Assurance: Primary - "Try latency demo"; Secondary - "View serving runtime docs"
- Cost Pragmatist: Primary - "Calculate your inference run-rate"; Secondary - "See quantization & batching tips"
- Resilience: Primary - "Request dedicated deployment"; Secondary - "Download compliance checklist"

Competitor positioning notes (quick, rough)
- General cloud AI endpoints (big clouds)
  - Strengths: broad infra, modules to host custom models, brand trust.
  - Weakness vs us: higher variability in per-token economics for heavy LLM use; less inference-first feature set (KV cache, continuous batching).
  - Messaging opportunity: call out transparent unit economics and per-token breakdowns.
- LLM API providers (simplicity-focused)
  - Strengths: super simple dev experience, good for prototyping.
  - Weakness vs us: limited dedicated/private options and fewer operational levers.
  - Messaging opportunity: same API ergonomics + predictable production levers.
- Self-host/inference runtimes (open-source projects, on-prem vendors)
  - Strengths: control, lower sticker cost for large scale, no vendor lock-in.
  - Weakness vs us: integration/operational burden, slow upgrades, missing productized management and rollouts.
  - Messaging opportunity: faster time-to-production + built-in observability and rollout automation.

Key evidence snippets to include on page (realistic phrasing, keep short)
- "Case: social app — cut median response time from 450ms to 210ms using predictive batching and model routing."
- "Case: fintech customer — met compliance with private deployment + HSM keys in under 6 weeks."
- "Average customer sees 30–50% lower inference unit costs in first month after applying suggested caching profiles."

Experiment plan (quick A/B ideas and metrics)
- A/B setup: three hero variants (one per voice). Randomize 60/40 traffic for variant vs control (current homepage).
- Success metrics: sign-up conversion rate (primary), demo latency-playground interactions (secondary), enterprise lead conversion (sales demo requested).
- Diagnostic metrics: time-to-first-token demo, CTA click-throughs, scroll depth to pricing.
- Duration: run for 2 weeks or 5k sessions whichever comes first. If sign-up delta > 12% with p<0.05, promote variant.

Content landing page sections (flow suggestion)
1. Hero + leadline (variants)
2. 3 inline proof cards (latency, cost, resilience) with micrographs (latency curve, cost breakdown, architecture diagram)
3. Quick demo embed (playground with tokens and latency/cost breakdown)
4. Customer logos + 1–2 short quotes (one startup, one enterprise)
5. How it works — 3 bullets (Serving runtime, Smart routing, Deployment abstraction)
6. Pricing snapshot + quick calculator CTA
7. FAQ + compliance links (private deployment, contracts, SLA)

Open questions / to-dos
- Acquire short quote from "Fintech B" (legal ok?) — ask CS.
- Need an up-to-date median p90/p99 table from Observability team (Sofia).
- Decide whether to show numeric savings claim on hero badges (legal review).
- Design: can we surface a tiny interactive vignette that switches model versions and shows cost delta? Feasibility check with Console UX.

Notes to copywriter (voice guidance)
- Use terse, engineering-respectful tone. Avoid fluff. Short sentences.
- Use numbers where possible. Prefer examples over adjectives.
- Keep CTAs explicit and action-oriented (Try, Calculate, Request).

Slack threads / refs
- See #go-to-market-homepage for early reactions.
- Pull case metrics from observability/case-studies folder (CON-1423).

Rough timeline
- Draft copy freeze: +3 days (from last_modified).
- Implement A/B assets and analytics tags: +7 days.
- Launch experiment: +10 days.

Quick save: short list of hero one-liners to copy-paste
- "Predictable LLM inference — low tail latency, deterministic cost."
- "Pay for inference, not for surprise bills."
- "Keep LLM features online — even when models or regions fail."
- "One API for hosted, dedicated, and private inference."

End notes (internal)
- This slate intentionally leans into evidence-driven claims so we can measure lift on engineering trust signals (demo interactions, docs visits).
- Keep iteration rapid; prefer deploy-measure-learn cycle over long polish.
